question.text: What is 'Rho' in the context of option Greeks?

answer.text: Rho measures the sensitivity of option premium to changes in the risk-free interest rate — call options have positive Rho (higher rates increase call value) and put options have negative Rho (higher rates decrease put value)
Rho measures the sensitivity of option premium to changes in the underlying stock price
Rho is the same as delta but for put options only
Rho has no practical significance and is never used in trading

explanation.text: The Logic: Rho is the change in option price for a one percentage point change in the risk-free interest rate. Calls generally have positive Rho (higher rates increase call value) while puts generally have negative Rho (higher rates decrease put value). The Trap: Price sensitivity to the underlying is delta, not Rho. Rho applies to both calls and puts but with opposite signs. Note: Rho is the source-supported definition for the change in option premium per unit change in the risk-free interest rate.
